sections.h2: Where do Pike County property tax payments go?
sections.html:
Pike County taxes are paid to the sheriff's Tax Division in Pikeville, at 146 Main Street, Suite 204. The main number is 606-432-6260 and the tax line is 606-432-6212. Mail goes to the Pike County Sheriff's Office, Tax Division, P.O. Box 839, Pikeville, KY 41502, with checks made out to "Pike County Sheriff."

Ways to pay the Pike County Sheriff, as posted on the sheriff's "Pay Your Taxes" page
Payment typeWhere it is accepted
CashIn person
Check or money orderIn person or by mail
Visa or MastercardIn person, by phone or online
Cash AppIn person, by phone or online

Online payment adds a 3% convenience fee on credit and debit cards, and the card statement shows the charge as "Kentucky Land Records." Search for the bill by number or by name, tick the box beside it, and press pay. Ask the Pike County Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) about values and exemptions, because the sheriff only collects.

sections.h2: What is the Pike County property tax schedule?
sections.html:
Pike County follows Kentucky's statewide timetable. A 2% discount applies when the bill is paid in full by November 1, face amount is due through December 31, and January brings a 5% penalty. Payment after January 31 carries a 10% penalty under KRS 134.015. Taxes count as a personal debt of the owner from the day they come due.

Call the Tax Division for the exact mailing date, because it shifts from year to year and a delayed year uses a month-by-month schedule. Revenue says the sheriff's books close at the end of business on April 15, which is the cut-off for what the clerk inherits. Because the deed carries an in-care-of address for the bill in the year of transfer, give the closing agent a mailing address that will still work after the sale.

sections.h2: How do Pike County owners appeal a valuation?
sections.html:
The path begins at the PVA's counter, since Kentucky does not allow an appeal until the owner has met the PVA or a deputy. The appeal itself is filed with the county clerk by the close of the workday after roll inspection ends. Inspection runs thirteen days from the first Monday in May, and the local board follows 25 to 35 days later.

  • Bring evidence: sales of similar homes, insurance policies, a contractor's repair estimate, photographs.
  • A paid representative must hold a qualifying professional credential, such as attorney, CPA or certified appraiser, and carry the owner's written authorization.
  • An owner may record the board hearing on audio.

The board must explain in writing any value it raises or lowers. A supplemental bill follows if the final number exceeds what the owner claimed.

sections.h2: How much does the homestead exemption save in Pike County?
sections.html: Eligible owners are people 65 and up, along with anyone classed as totally disabled. For 2025 and 2026 they subtract $49,100 from the assessed value. A home worth Pike County's Census median of $112,000 would be taxed on $62,900 afterward. The PVA takes the application, and a birth certificate, license or passport proves age.

sections.h2: What happens when a Pike County tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
At the end of April 15, the sheriff's unpaid bills move to the Pike County Clerk, at which point they are certificates of delinquency and a lien is recorded. Interest begins at one percent a month, and a clerk fee and county attorney fee are added. The county attorney's first notice goes out within 30 days and a second within 60, and the clerk must advertise the list in the newspaper beforehand.

For a county on the normal schedule, the sale can be set on any business day from July 14 through August 28. Clerks who also sell delinquent oil, gas or unmined mineral bills get 60 more days, with a deadline of October 27. Pike County has large coal and natural gas reserves, so a seller with mineral interests should ask the clerk whether any such bill is attached. A seller who still owes a bill should get a payoff from the clerk before listing, since a certificate bought by an investor adds substantial fees.

sections.h2: What will a Pike County seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
The grantor owes the transfer tax, which works out to a half dollar for every $500 block of the deed's price (KRS 142.050). A sale at the $112,000 median would owe $112.00. The Pike County Clerk lists a deed at $50 and a mortgage at $80, with $3 added per page past the fifth for a deed.

The clerk can be reached at 606-432-6211. The Pikeville office serves Monday through Thursday from 8:30 to 4:30 and Friday from 8:30 to 5:30. Three branch offices keep shorter schedules:

  • Belfry: Tuesday 9:00 to 4:00 and Friday 9:00 to 6:00.
  • Phelps: Monday 9:00 to 4:00 and Wednesday 9:00 to 5:30.
  • Elkhorn City: Tuesday 9:00 to 4:00 and Thursday 9:00 to 5:30.

The clerk's deed page lists what a deed must carry, including a notarized consideration statement and an address for the next tax bill, so ask the closing agent to check the form first.

sections.h2: What is Pike County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Pike County is Kentucky's easternmost county and its largest by land area, at 786.73 square miles in the 2020 Census. Pikeville is the seat, and Elkhorn City and Coal Run Village are the other cities. The county was created in 1821 from part of Floyd County and named for explorer Zebulon Pike. Since 2019 its fiscal court has been made of three commissioners and the judge/executive, after voters approved the change in 2016. Pikeville became a city and the seat in 1893, and U.S. 23 passes through the Pikeville Cut-Through, a massive earthmoving project.

Coal and natural gas built the economy, and Pike ranked second in Kentucky coal output in 2013. Health care now matters just as much: the Census Bureau counts $1.06 billion in 2022 receipts from health care and social services, and Pikeville Medical Center and the University of Pikeville sit in the county seat. The county has five high school systems under Pike County Schools (Belfry, East Ridge, Phelps, Pike County Central and Shelby Valley) plus Pikeville Independent Schools. Big Sandy Community and Technical College and Galen College of Nursing both have Pikeville campuses.

Visitors come for Breaks Interstate Park on the Kentucky-Virginia line, shows at the Eastern Kentucky Exposition Center, which opened in 2005 with 7,000 seats, and plays at the Jenny Wiley Theatre's downtown Pikeville stage, opened in 2014. Pike borders Martin, Floyd, Letcher and Knott counties in Kentucky, Mingo County in West Virginia, and Buchanan, Dickenson and Wise counties in Virginia.

  • Population fell from 58,669 in 2020 to an estimated 54,721 in 2025, a 6.7% drop.
  • The 2020 census listed 28,693 housing units, 14.5% of them vacant, and 28.0% of occupied homes were rentals.
  • QuickFacts shows 29,481 housing units in 2025, a median gross rent of $858 and median owner costs of $1,278 with a mortgage.
  • Median household income is $44,312, and 22.4% of residents live in poverty.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Pike County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Pike County Sheriff's Tax Division, 146 Main Street, Suite 204, Pikeville, or by mail to P.O. Box 839. The tax line is 606-432-6212.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for paying Pike County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Yes, a 3% convenience fee applies to credit and debit cards, and the charge appears as Kentucky Land Records.

faqs.q: What is the Pike County transfer tax on a $112,000 sale?
faqs.a: It is $112.00. The seller pays 50 cents per $500 of value, and the clerk collects it before recording the deed.

faqs.q: When do unpaid Pike County bills reach the clerk?
faqs.a: After the close of business on April 15, when the sheriff transfers them to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency.

faqs.q: Where is the Pike County Clerk's office?
faqs.a: The clerk's number is 606-432-6211, with offices in Pikeville, Belfry, Phelps and Elkhorn City, each on its own weekly schedule.
